What is the difference between SEO and AEO?
−
SEO helps search engines find, understand and rank your pages. AEO shapes the same content so that clear, well-supported answers are easier for answer systems to interpret and possibly surface. They overlap heavily: helpful content and a healthy website help both.
How long can SEO take to show results?
+
It depends on the competition, the condition of the site, the quality of the content and how often changes are made. Some technical fixes show effects sooner, while content and authority usually take longer to build. We do not promise a fixed timeline.
Can you optimize an existing website?
+
Yes. We start with an assessment of the current site, then fix what holds it back and improve what already works, without rebuilding it unless that is really needed.
Do you provide technical SEO and content SEO?
+
Yes. Technical SEO, on-page work, keyword research, content strategy and optimization, local SEO and AEO are all part of our scope, depending on what your site needs.
Can you help improve AI search visibility?
+
We can help you make your information clearer, more consistent and easier to crawl, which can make it more eligible to be used in AI-generated answers. No one can guarantee inclusion in them.
How is SEO progress measured?
+
Where tracking is set up, we look at organic clicks and impressions, query performance, indexed pages, landing-page engagement and relevant conversions, and we keep activity metrics separate from business outcomes.
Do you guarantee search rankings?
+
No. Rankings depend on competition, technical condition, content quality, authority and many other factors, some of which we do not control. We commit to careful, ethical work and clear reporting, not to a ranking position.

Behind

A website, an app or a virtual world looks like technology. It is really a long list of small decisions, made by people who care.
The way a button feels, the way a page loads, the way a 3D model moves:
somebody thought about every one of them.
At We3vision that somebody sits in our office in Surat. They are developers, designers, 3D artists, engineers and marketers, and they have been building together since 2019. We do not hide them behind a company name. This page is here to introduce them.
Tools change every year. What does not change is that good work comes from people who listen, disagree kindly, help each other and finish what they start. That is why the team comes first at We3vision, and the projects come after.
We move forward because they move forward. Every project we ship is a thank-you to the people who built it.

Our values
What
we
believe
in
as
a
team
Not words on a wall. These are the habits you will see in our office every day.
01
People before projects
A project ends, a person stays. We look after the team first, because a team that is looked after looks after its clients.
02
Together, not one after the other
Designers, developers and artists work on the same problem at the same time. The best idea wins, whoever it came from.
03
Own it from start to finish
Everyone owns something real: a screen, a module, a client. If it is yours, you finish it and you fix it.
04
Keep learning
AR, VR, AI and new frameworks: the field moves fast, so learning is part of the work, not a favour.
05
Be honest, and be kind
We tell clients what is possible and what is not. We tell each other what works and what does not.
06
Make it simple
Clear layouts, clear words, clear promises. If a user has to think twice, we are not done.
Growing together
How
we
help
the
people
grow
A company moves forward only when its people do. This is what we try to give everybody who joins us.
01
Real projects from the first weeks
New people work on live projects with a mentor next to them, not on practice tasks.
02
Mentors in every team
Senior people, our founders among them, guide the younger ones, in the metaverse team and beyond.
03
Room to go deep
Web, mobile, AI, VR, 3D, brand or marketing: you can grow in the field you love.
04
Credit where it is due
Good work is named and shown, on this page and on our projects.
05
A team that helps
Stuck? Ask. Somebody in the office has been there before and will sit down with you.
06
A path upward
People grow with the company, from their first project to leading one.

01
Where is the We3vision team based?
Our head office and development team are in Surat, Gujarat, India. We also have an office in Marburg, Germany.
02
Who will I talk to when I start a project?
You get one main contact, a project manager, who knows everything about your project. Designers and developers join the calls whenever it helps.
03
What kind of people work at We3vision?
Web and mobile developers, UI/UX and graphic designers, 2D/3D animators, AR/VR and Unity engineers, AI engineers, QA engineers, SEO specialists and content writers.
04
Can I join the team?
Yes. Look at the open roles on our Careers page, or write to hr@we3vision.com with your work and a few words about you.
05
Do you work with clients outside India?
Yes. We work with companies across India and the globe, and we have an office in Germany.

AI Agents for Business: What They Are and Where They Save Time
October 9, 2026
AI agents do more than answer questions: they read, decide and act inside your tools. See what they are, where they pay off first and how to start safely.
Most businesses first meet AI as a chatbot that answers questions. An AI agent goes a step further: it understands a request, looks at the right information and then does the work inside your tools.
What is an AI agent?
An AI agent is software built around a language model that can use tools. Give it a goal, such as "qualify this new enquiry", and it can read the message, look up the customer in your CRM, score the lead, reply and create a task for your sales team.
The key difference from a normal script is that the agent copes with messy, human input. Emails, voice notes and forms never look the same twice, and an agent can still work out what is being asked.
Where agents save time first
The best first jobs are repetitive, rule-based and high-volume:
Answering the same customer questions at any hour.
Sorting and routing incoming emails and enquiries.
Entering data from invoices, forms and documents into your system.
Writing weekly reports from numbers that already exist.
Chasing follow-ups so no lead is forgotten.
How an agent works
Behind the scenes there are four parts. The model understands language. The tools are the actions it may take, such as search, update or send. The memory holds what it needs to know about your business. The rules say what it must never do and when a person has to approve.
Good agents are boring in the best way: they do a narrow job reliably and hand the difficult cases to your team with the full context.
How to start safely
Pick one workflow that wastes real hours today.
Write down the steps a human follows, including the exceptions.
Give the agent only the access it needs.
Keep a person in the loop for payments, refunds and anything legal.
Measure time saved and mistakes for a month before you add more.
What to avoid
Do not start with "an AI for everything". A vague goal gives vague results. Do not skip testing with real examples, and do not hide the agent: customers should know when they are talking to an automated assistant and be able to reach a person.
Getting help
At We3vision we design and build custom AI agents that connect to your website, CRM and documents. If you have a workflow that eats your team's day, tell us about it and we will suggest what an agent can take over.
Frequently asked questions
What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
A chatbot answers questions in a conversation. An AI agent can also take actions: it checks your CRM, updates a record, books a meeting or sends a message, following rules you set.
Are AI agents safe for customer data?
They can be, when they only get the access they need, actions are logged and a person approves the sensitive steps. Security is part of the design, not an extra.
How long does it take to build one?
A focused agent for one workflow can often be live in a few weeks. A larger system with several tools takes longer, so start with one clear job.

Native vs Cross-Platform Apps: Flutter, React Native or Swift/Kotlin?
October 7, 2026
Native, Flutter or React Native? Compare cost, speed, performance and maintenance, and choose the right way to build your Android and iOS app.
One of the first decisions in an app project is how to build it. The choice affects cost, speed to launch and what the app can do. Here is a clear comparison.
Native apps
Native means writing separate apps: Swift or Objective-C for iOS, Kotlin or Java for Android. You get full access to every feature of the phone and the smoothest possible behaviour, at the price of two code bases and two sets of work.
Cross-platform apps
Cross-platform frameworks let one team build one app for both systems.
Flutter draws its own interface with a fast engine and gives very consistent design on every device.
React Native uses native interface parts controlled from JavaScript and suits teams that already know React.
What to compare
Cost: cross-platform usually needs less work overall.
Time to market: one code base means a faster first release and faster updates.
Performance: both are excellent for typical business apps; native leads for very heavy graphics or hardware use.
Look and feel: native follows each platform exactly; Flutter gives you one consistent custom design.
Maintenance: one code base is simpler to keep up to date.
Talent: consider who will maintain the app after launch.
Which one fits which app?
Business, booking, e-commerce and content apps: cross-platform is a strong choice.
Apps with advanced camera, AR, Bluetooth or heavy 3D: consider native, or a hybrid where only those parts are native.
An internal tool for staff: cross-platform or even a web app may be enough.
Do you need an app at all?
If your visitors mainly browse and buy occasionally, a fast mobile website or a progressive web app may serve them well. An app makes sense when people return often, you need notifications or you use phone features.
Plan beyond launch
Budget for updates when new phone versions arrive, for fixing bugs and for improving the app with user feedback.
Let's decide together
We3vision builds Android and iOS apps in the technology that fits the product. Describe your idea and your users and we will recommend an approach and a first release plan.
Frequently asked questions
Is a cross-platform app slower than a native one?
For most business apps the difference is not noticeable. Apps with heavy graphics, advanced camera or sensors may benefit from native code.
Which is cheaper to build?
A cross-platform app usually costs less because one code base serves Android and iOS, but the final cost depends on features.
Can I start with one platform?
Yes. Many businesses launch on the platform most of their customers use and add the other later.

Getting people to use it
Agree one rule: "If it is not in the CRM, it did not happen." Train the team in a short session, review the pipeline together weekly and remove any step that feels like paperwork.

Buying a tool with too many features.
Not assigning an owner for the system.

How to Build a Custom AI Chatbot for Your Website, Step by Step
October 1, 2026
A practical, non-technical guide to planning, building and launching an AI chatbot that answers from your own content and hands over to your team when needed.
A chatbot is often the first AI project a business tries. Done well, it answers visitors instantly, collects leads and lightens the load on your team. Done badly, it frustrates people. Here is how to do it well.
Step 1: decide what the chatbot is for
Write one sentence: "This chatbot helps visitors to ___." Typical goals are answering product questions, booking a call, checking an order or qualifying a lead. One clear goal beats five vague ones.
Step 2: collect the knowledge
The chatbot is only as good as what it knows. Gather your FAQs, service pages, price information, policies and common email answers. Remove anything outdated or contradictory before you start.
Step 3: choose the approach
Rule-based flows: buttons and fixed paths. Predictable, but limited.
AI chatbot with retrieval: it reads your content and writes natural answers based on it.
AI agent: also takes actions, such as creating a ticket or booking a meeting.
Most businesses are best served by an AI chatbot grounded in their own content, with a few actions added later.
Step 4: design the conversation
Decide the tone, the first message and what happens when the bot does not know. A good answer to "I am not sure" is a hand-over: "I will pass this to our team, may I take your e-mail?"
Step 5: connect it to your tools
Link it to your website, CRM, e-mail and calendar so that a conversation turns into a lead or a booking, not a dead end.
Step 6: test with real questions
Collect fifty real questions from e-mails and calls and run them through. Fix the weak answers, then repeat. Test the unhappy paths too: rude messages, off-topic questions and requests it must refuse.
Step 7: launch, watch and improve
Start with a small share of traffic, read the conversations weekly and add missing knowledge. A chatbot is a living product, not a one-off project.
Common mistakes
Promising too much in the first message.
Hiding the way to reach a person.
Letting it answer about prices or legal terms without approved content.
Need one built?
We3vision builds custom chatbots and AI assistants that sit on your website and connect to your systems. Share what your visitors ask most and we will show you what is possible.
Frequently asked questions
Do I need my own data to build a chatbot?
It helps. A chatbot works best when it can read your own pages, FAQs, price lists and documents so its answers match your business.
Can the chatbot capture leads?

Follow the full journey of building a mobile app: discovery, design, development, testing, launch and updates, with what to expect at each step.
Building an app is a journey with clear stages. Knowing them helps you plan, budget and make decisions at the right time.
1. Discovery
We define the problem, the users, the goals and the success measures. This is the time to decide what the first version must do and what can wait.
2. Research and planning
Study similar apps, list features, order them by value and effort, and agree on a first release. A short, honest list beats a long wish list.
3. UX and flows
Sketch how a person moves through the app: sign-up, finding things, completing the main task. Wireframes let you test the logic before any design is drawn.
4. UI design
Colours, typography, icons and screens come together in a design that matches your brand and feels natural on a phone. A clickable prototype lets you try it before it is built.
5. Development
Engineers build the app and its back end: database, APIs, accounts, notifications and admin tools. Work is shared in short cycles so you see progress regularly.
6. Testing
Test on real devices, different screen sizes and weak connections. Check what happens when something goes wrong, not only when everything works.
7. Launch
Prepare the store listings, screenshots, descriptions and privacy information, and submit to the stores. Review times vary, so allow for them.
8. After launch
Watch crashes, usage and reviews. Plan updates, fix problems quickly and add features based on what people actually do.
How to be a good client
Name one decision maker.
Give feedback in rounds, not drip by drip.
Provide content and brand materials on time.
Be open to trimming scope to launch sooner.
Ready to start?
We3vision guides you through every stage, from the first sketch to the store. Tell us about your idea and we will outline the steps and a realistic first release.

How long does an app take to build?
A focused first version often takes a few months. Larger products with many features and integrations take longer.
What is an MVP?
A minimum viable product: the smallest version that solves the main problem, so you can learn from real users before building more.
Who owns the code?
You should. Agree ownership and handover of source code, accounts and documentation in writing at the start.

Should you buy a ready-made CRM or build your own? Compare cost, fit, speed and long-term value to choose the option that suits your business.
Ready-made CRMs are quick to start. Custom CRMs are built around your process. Neither wins every time; the right answer depends on how you work.
Ready-made CRM
Fast to start, often within days.
Proven features and regular updates.
Monthly cost per user, which grows with your team.
Customisation is possible but within the limits of the product.
Custom CRM
Built around your exact workflow, fields and rules.
Integrates deeply with your other systems.
You own it and are not limited by someone else's roadmap.
Higher cost and time at the beginning, and a team to maintain it.
Questions that decide it
How unusual is your sales process? Standard processes fit standard tools.
How many users will you have, and how fast will that grow?
How many other systems must it talk to?
Do you handle sensitive data that must stay in a specific place?
Will you have a technical partner to maintain it?
A middle road
You can use a ready-made CRM and extend it: custom fields, automation, integrations and a few purpose-built modules. This often gives most of the benefit with a smaller investment.
Think in total cost
Compare three to five years, not the first month. Include licences, setup, training, integrations, maintenance and the cost of working around limits.
Signs you have outgrown a ready-made tool
You pay for many seats that barely use it.
You keep spreadsheets next to it for things it cannot do.
Important processes need manual steps between systems.
Get a recommendation
We3vision builds custom CRM and ERP software and also implements standard tools. We will compare both for your case, with a clear estimate of time and cost.

Is a custom CRM always more expensive?
It costs more to start but has no per-user licence growth. Over several years the numbers depend on your team size and needs.
Can I start with ready-made and move later?
Yes. Many companies begin with a standard tool and build custom parts or a full system when they outgrow it.
Who owns a custom CRM?
You should own the code and data. Agree this clearly in the contract.

How to Build a Brand Identity: Logo, Colours and Voice

A brand identity is more than a logo. Learn the parts that make a brand recognisable: purpose, visuals, voice and the rules that keep them consistent.
A brand is the picture people carry in their heads about your business. A brand identity is the set of visible and audible signals that create that picture. A logo is part of it, but never the whole.
Start with the foundation
Before colours and shapes, answer a few questions in writing:
Who do we serve, and what do they care about?
What do we do better or differently?
Three words that describe how we want to be seen.
Who are we not?
The visual identity
Logo: simple, memorable and flexible. It should work small, in one colour and on a dark or light background.
Colour: a main colour, a few supporting ones and neutral tones. Colours carry emotion, so choose with your audience in mind.
Typography: readable fonts that match your personality.
Imagery and graphics: the style of photos, icons and illustration.
Layout: spacing and grids that make your materials feel related.
The verbal identity
Name and tagline.
Tone of voice: friendly, expert, playful or serious.
Key messages: the few lines you repeat everywhere.
Bring it together in a guide
A brand guide records the rules and examples: logo clear space, colour codes, font sizes and sample layouts. It keeps your team and your suppliers consistent.
Roll it out
Website and social profiles.
Stationery and documents.
Packaging and signage.
Presentations and sales materials.
Uniforms or vehicles, if you have them.
Pitfalls
Trend-chasing logos that date quickly, too many variations, and a brand that looks good in a presentation but cannot be used in daily work.
Build yours with us
We3vision creates brand identities from research and strategy to logo, guidelines and applications. Tell us about your business and we will show you how a clear identity can work for it.

What is the difference between a logo and a brand identity?
The logo is one element. A brand identity includes colours, typography, imagery, voice and rules for using them.
How long does a branding project take?
Often several weeks, depending on research, the number of design rounds and the number of materials.
Do I need a brand strategy first?
A clear idea of who you serve and what makes you different makes the design much stronger.

RAG Explained: Let AI Answer From Your Own Documents
September 24, 2026
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets an AI answer using your own documents instead of guessing. Learn how it works, where it fits and what it needs.
Ask a general AI a question about your company and it may sound confident and still be wrong. It was never given your price list, your contracts or your internal guides. RAG fixes this.
What is RAG?
RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation. In plain words: before the AI answers, the system searches your own documents for the most relevant passages and hands them to the AI together with the question. The AI then writes the answer from that material.
Think of an assistant who looks things up in your handbook before replying, instead of answering from memory.
How it works
Your documents are split into small pieces and stored in a searchable index.
When someone asks a question, the system finds the pieces closest in meaning.
Those pieces and the question go to the language model.
The model writes an answer and can point to the sources it used.
Where RAG is useful
A support assistant that answers from your help articles and manuals.
An internal assistant for policies, HR questions and onboarding.
A sales assistant that knows your products, specifications and case studies.
Search across contracts, reports and proposals in natural language.
What you need to make it work
Clean content. Old, duplicated or conflicting documents produce confusing answers.
Clear access rules, so people only see what they are allowed to see.
A way to measure quality: a list of real questions with the answers you expect.
A plan to keep the index fresh when documents change.
RAG compared with fine-tuning
Fine-tuning changes the model itself and is useful for style or specialised tasks. RAG leaves the model alone and gives it fresh facts at the moment of the question. For business knowledge that changes, RAG is usually faster to build and easier to update.
Pitfalls
Poorly split documents, missing tables and scanned pages without text recognition are the usual causes of bad answers. Plan some time for preparing the data; it matters more than the choice of model.
Start with one knowledge base
Pick one body of knowledge your team repeats every day, build a pilot, test it with real questions and expand from there. We3vision can help you design and build it, from document preparation to a working assistant.
Frequently asked questions
What does RAG stand for?
Retrieval-augmented generation: the AI first retrieves the relevant parts of your documents, then writes an answer based on them.
Does RAG stop the AI from making things up?
It greatly reduces it, because the answer is grounded in your content, and good systems can show the source. It does not remove the need for testing.
Is my data used to train public models?
That depends on how it is built. A well-designed system keeps your documents in your own store and uses them only to answer your questions.

UI/UX Design Principles That Turn Visitors Into Customers
September 22, 2026
Good design is not decoration. These practical UI/UX principles make your website clearer, easier to use and better at turning visitors into customers.
People do not read websites; they scan them. Good UI/UX design respects this and makes the next step obvious. These principles apply to almost every business website.
1. Make the purpose clear in five seconds
A visitor should understand what you offer, who it is for and what to do next without scrolling or thinking. Use a clear headline, a short supporting line and one main button.
2. Create a visual hierarchy
Size, colour, spacing and position tell people what matters. One main message per section, with supporting details quieter, guides the eye.
3. Keep navigation simple
Use familiar labels and a small number of choices. Visitors should always know where they are and how to get back.
4. Write for scanning
Short paragraphs, descriptive headings and lists help people find what they came for. Use plain language, not jargon.
5. One main action per page
Pages with five equal buttons confuse. Decide the primary action and make it stand out; keep secondary actions visible but quieter.
6. Reduce friction in forms
Ask only what you need, show clear labels, explain errors helpfully and make the button say what happens next.
7. Build trust
Show real faces, client logos with permission, results, clear contact details and policies. Small details of care add up to confidence.
8. Design for speed and for all people
Fast pages, readable text, enough contrast and support for keyboard and screen readers help everyone, not only some users.
9. Test with real people
Five users completing a task will reveal problems your team cannot see. Test early with sketches, then again with the real thing.
10. Improve continuously
Use analytics, recordings and feedback to find where people stop, then change one thing at a time.
Want a fresh look at your site?
We3vision offers UI/UX design and reviews. Send us your pages and we will point out the changes most likely to help your visitors act.
Frequently asked questions
What is the difference between UI and UX?
UI is how the product looks and feels: layout, colours and controls. UX is the whole experience: how easy it is to reach a goal.
Can design really improve sales?
Clear structure, readable text and a simple path to action remove friction, which often leads to more enquiries and purchases.
How do I know what to fix first?
Watch real users, check where they leave in your analytics and start with the pages closest to the sale.
